# Cedar Valley Evacuation Operations Decision

## Decision, scope, and authority
The county incident commander holds sole legal authority to issue evacuation orders after receiving fire-behavior recommendations [S01]. Supporting branches (sheriff, public health, shelter) execute specific functions but cannot independently declare readiness [S01]. Vendors, dashboards, and model recommendations are advisory only and lack closure authority [S01][S16]. Authority transfers at shift change require acknowledged incident-action-plan revisions; unacknowledged handoffs block new readiness declarations [S01]. The decision covers a 48-hour operational sequence from warning through evacuation, sheltering, accountability, verification, and readiness. Scope includes Zones A-North, A-River, B-East, B-Center, C-South, and C-Ridge [S01]. Readiness requires resolution of all hard blockers, effect incorporation, current integrated check, and incident-command acceptance [S16]. Submission or model-authored ledgers do not constitute readiness authority [S16]. The candidate package must satisfy all criteria before IC acceptance [S16]. This decision binds the operational sequence to observed source evidence rather than nominal capacity claims.

## Hazard triggers and zone sequencing
Conservative fire and weather triggers govern mandatory evacuation, distinct from voluntary warnings [S02]. Zone A triggers require action within 6 hours; Zones B and C follow sequential timing based on wind-shift ensemble data [S15]. Forecast binding uses conservative ensemble values, not median forecasts, to avoid delay [S02][S15]. The 5.8 km/h sustained wind threshold combined with 42 percent relative humidity represents the conservative trigger point for Zone A mandatory order [S02]. Expiry requires explicit cancellation by the incident commander [S01]. Zone sequencing follows: A-North, A-River (mandatory), then B-East, B-Center, C-South, C-Ridge [S01]. One zone revision is permitted under IC authority if forecast updates warrant [S01][S15]. The 42 percent humidity threshold ensures conservative activation without median forecast delay [S02]. Smoke exposure thresholds from S11 must also inform relocation decisions when PM2.5 exceeds 150 micrograms per cubic meter [S11].

## Population, transport, and route clearance
Zone populations are: A: 5,280; B: 8,940; C: 12,600, plus tourist estimates [S03]. Medical assistance categories (mobility, oxygen, etc.) overlap and must not be summed as distinct individuals [S03]. Survey coverage is incomplete, requiring uncertainty allowances for clearance demand [S03]. Mill Junction is a shared bottleneck; capacities of feeding roads cannot be summed [S04]. Observed exercise throughput is 1,180 veh/h [S04][S13]. Contraflow requires sheriff closure and setup time [S04]. Route-loss contingencies require alternative paths validated by current checks [S04]. Fleet reservation must match person/accommodation needs [S03]. Emergency inbound capacity for medical and rescue vehicles must be preserved during evacuation operations [S04]. The nineteen percent uncertainty allowance applies to tourist population estimates in Zones B and C [S03]. Eighteen county buses exist, but only eleven qualified drivers can report within two hours [S05]. Four lift-equipped buses carry thirty-four seated riders each in that configuration [S05]. Twelve school buses become available at 14:30 after student release and cannot be assumed in earlier Zone A clearance [S05]. Drivers have a twelve-hour duty ceiling, and a route plan using every driver for outbound movement leaves no legal return, relief, or shelter-transfer capacity [S05]. Ambulances are reserved for clinical need and are not general mobility vehicles [S05]. Person-level oxygen matching requires public health to bind each high-acuity person to transport, destination, power, medication custody, and handoff confirmation [S07]. Seventy-three residents use continuous oxygen, twenty-eight have dialysis due within twenty-four hours, and fourteen medications require refrigeration [S07]. The lists overlap and contain seven duplicate household records [S07]. Cedar Hospital can accept twenty-two oxygen-dependent evacuees, North Clinic thirty-seven, and verified home oxygen kits cover twenty more [S07]. Those capacities total seventy-nine only if transport, power, and patient matching all pass [S07]. A generic shelter cot is not a medical placement [S07].

## Shelter, medical, and accessibility continuity
Smoke-safe shelter capacity requirements define minimum filtration standards [S06]. Accessible placements must match person/accommodation needs identified in population surveys [S03][S06]. Medical handoffs require public health ownership [S01][S16]. Ridge School filter repair remains incomplete [S16]. Person-level oxygen matching is unresolved [S16]. Shelter relocation triggers activate if filtration fails or capacity exceeds limits [S06]. Power continuity for medical equipment requires backup generators with staged fuel [S09]. The nineteen percent survey uncertainty in Zone C requires additional accessible placement reservation [S03][S07]. Lift chair transport must be matched to person-level mobility needs without double-counting [S05][S07]. Outdoor PM2.5 above 150 micrograms per cubic meter triggers relocation of unfiltered shelters [S11]. Above 250, field loading requires respiratory protection and shorter staging intervals [S11]. Ridge School failed its last filter inspection [S11]. Civic Arena and West College passed with MERV-13 filters; Expo Hall has only eighty percent of required replacement filters on site [S11]. The smoke model can make an otherwise distant shelter unusable before fire arrival [S11]. Distance from flame is not a complete shelter-safety criterion [S11]. A filter replacement changes the candidate resource state and requires a current inspection, not reuse of the prior readiness check [S11].

## Warnings, accountability, and community support
Redundant multilingual warning channels are mandatory [S08]. Door-knock timing aligns with zone sequencing to ensure receipt before mandatory order [S03][S08]. Radio interoperability is a blocking blocker; volunteer-radio identifier test remains incomplete [S16]. Receipt/understanding evidence requires community support mechanisms [S08]. Private accountability records maintain restricted medical data; public aggregation excludes sensitive health information [S12]. Self-evacuation verification occurs without publishing destinations [S12]. Retention and deletion proofs are mandatory for operational rosters [S12]. Hmong language materials must be available in all warning channels [S08]. The nineteen percent uncertainty requires redundant channel verification for Zone C residents [S03][S08]. Public status messages may not expose health needs; the private roster rules in S12 govern matching and deletion [S07]. Require person-level private matching with aggregate public reporting [S07]. Treat any unmatched oxygen, dialysis, or refrigerated-medication case as a blocker [S07].

## Power, fuel, and resource contracting
Fuel and power continuity requirements address observed delays in resupply [S09]. Local staging of fuel reserves mitigates delay risks [S09]. Alternate routes and suppliers require confirmation; alternate fuel confirmation remains a blocker [S16]. Coupled asset effects (e.g., fuel shortages impacting medical generators) are not fully resolved [S16]. Resource contracting authority rests with the incident commander for emergency procurement [S01]. Cost ceilings apply to emergency contracts [S14]. The observed delay of nineteen hours in primary fuel delivery requires staged reserves at each zone checkpoint [S09]. Lift equipment power requirements must be addressed in generator staging [S05][S09]. Fuel endurance and delayed resupply constrain repeated cycles; nominal seats are not the same as sustained evacuation throughput [S05]. Reserve accessible capacity first, state cycle times, and preserve relief-driver capacity [S05]. Do not count unavailable school buses or unstaffed vehicles as operational capacity [S05].

## Forty-eight-hour execution and contingencies
Hour 0–2: IC issues voluntary warning; fire-behavior lead validates triggers [S01][S02]. Hour 2–6: Zone A-North mandatory order issued; sheriff executes traffic control; public health initiates medical continuity [S01]. Hour 6–12: Zone A-River evacuation begins; contraflow setup at Mill Junction [S04]. Hour 12–24: Zones B-East and B-Center evacuate; shelter intake peaks; fuel staging activates [S09]. Hour 24–36: Zones C-South and C-Ridge evacuate; accountability reconciliation begins [S12]. Hour 36–48: Verification, repair of blockers, recheck, and readiness assessment [S16]. Contingencies include route-loss activation of alternate paths [S04], shelter relocation if filtration fails [S06], and fuel diversion if primary supplier fails [S09]. The nineteen hour observed delay requires pre-positioned fuel at all staging points before mandatory order [S09]. If PM2.5 exceeds 150 micrograms per cubic meter, relocate unfiltered shelters immediately [S11]. If driver duty ceiling approaches twelve hours, activate relief drivers from reserve pool [S05].

## Verification, readiness, blockers, and falsifiers
Independent review classifies the package as not ready [S16]. Open blockers: North Bridge engineering inspection, complete driver roster, Ridge School filter repair, volunteer-radio identifier test, alternate fuel confirmation, and person-level oxygen matching [S16]. Component dashboards are green but bind to different plan revisions; no current integrated check exists [S16]. Readiness requires resolution of all hard blockers, effect incorporation, current recheck, and IC acceptance [S16]. Falsifiers: If any blocker remains open, the package is not ready. If a current integrated check does not cover zone order, routes, fleet, shelters, medical roster, communications, fuel, forecast, and accountability design together, readiness cannot be declared [S16]. The candidate must demonstrate all criteria met before submission can be considered for closure [S16]. Do not declare clean-air capacity from nominal building occupancy [S11]. Require person-level private matching with aggregate public reporting [S07]. Treat any unmatched oxygen, dialysis, or refrigerated-medication case as a blocker [S07].
